slot.brief: P–V diagram of a cyclic process (rectangle/triangle in P–V plane); ask for the net work done per cycle as the enclosed area.

stem: An ideal gas undergoes the cyclic process shown in the P-V diagram. The process consists of two isobaric and two isochoric steps. The net work done by the gas per cycle is (Take 1 atm = 10^5 Pa, 1 L = 10^-3 m^3):

verdicts.working: The cycle is counterclockwise, so net work done by the gas is minus the enclosed area: \(W=(2-5)(7-3)\,\text{atm·L}=-12\times10^5\times10^{-3}=-1200\,\text{J}\).
issues: The net work done by the gas is −1200 J, but no option gives this signed value; option C gives only its magnitude.

verdicts.working: Rectangle: ΔV = 4 L = 4e-3 m^3, ΔP = 3 atm = 3e5 Pa, area = 1200 J. Direction A→B→C→D is counterclockwise (expansion at low P, compression at high P), so the work done by the gas is actually −1200 J. The magnitude matches option C.
issues: The arrows show a counterclockwise cycle, so the net work done by the gas is −1200 J. Option C lists +1200 J, so the question is sloppy about sign and only the magnitude matches.

working:
Work per cycle equals the area enclosed by the P-V loop. Area = (7 - 3) L * (5 - 2) atm = 4 L * 3 atm = 12 L atm. Since 1 L atm = 10^-3 m^3 * 10^5 Pa = 100 J, work = 12 * 100 = 1200 J. Correct option is C.

Independent check: Rectangle: ΔV = 4 L = 4e-3 m^3, ΔP = 3 atm = 3e5 Pa, area = 1200 J. Direction A→B→C→D is counterclockwise (expansion at low P, compression at high P), so the work done by the gas is actually −1200 J. The magnitude matches option C.
solution:
Net work per cycle equals the area enclosed by the $P$–$V$ loop:
$$W=(7-3)(5-2)=12\ \text{L·atm}$$
Using $1\ \text{L·atm}=100\ \text{J}$, the enclosed work is $12\times100=1200\ \text{J}$. Note: if the stated counterclockwise direction is intended, work done by the gas is $-1200\ \text{J}$; the listed answer gives its magnitude.
